reader.job_to_be_done: Decide whether a game project deserves BD attention and what to do next.

report_contract.daily_report: Separate discovery from BD recommendation. Push pool can be empty. Non-dropped auto leads must enter the unprocessed inbox, not observation or follow-up buckets.
report_contract.steam_trends: Output Steam market-board intelligence, not sourcing-rule notes. It must cover category risers, Steam/Next Fest or demo windows, publisher/developer slate signals, public data quality, and concrete BD implications.
report_contract.industry_radar: Use real external media, company, legal, platform, or community signals. 行业新闻 is macro only; concrete games, recommendations, fun products, IP/company/legal gossip, and former 发行八卦 items belong in 今日亮点. Never use internal CRM notes as industry news.

push_pool_guardrails: Domestic products are the sourcing default because cooperation, efficiency, visual/cultural fit, and signing probability are materially better.
Domestic developer Demo/test signals must be promoted in priority and can override the old 60-day-only launch-window heuristic.
The launch window can be earlier and longer than 60 days; do not discard early domestic products merely because the release date is far away or imprecise.
Domestic unreleased products should follow a testing-first workflow: test or inspect the game before asking BD to complete contacts or long-form evidence.
Domestic near-window products should not be hard-dropped only because they are within 60 days when they are still unreleased and testable.
Overseas projects must not consume review slots unless they have clear PC data validation and a credible mobile-adaptation angle.
Already released projects must not enter push or watch candidates; they can only be dropped or used as market background.
PC Early Access projects must not enter push pool.
Narrative-first or visual-novel-like projects must not enter push pool by default.
India-led teams must not enter push pool.
Projects occupied by a mature publisher with China capability must not enter push pool by default.
Weak overseas projects without PC hit validation and mobile-adaptation potential must not enter push or watch candidates.
source_strategy: Expand domestic discovery through Chinese game/business media, domestic indie/developer communities, Bilibili video/search API signals, indienova, TapTap-style developer signals, and official studio posts.
Concrete product leads found through domestic media or Bilibili must enter the daily lead candidate pools with their original URLs, not only the industry radar.

Domestic media items containing a named game plus signals such as edition approval, first reveal, playtest, demo, trailer, store page, reservation, or domestic studio/publisher context should be treated as sourcing leads even when Steam data is missing.
Bilibili search results must point to a concrete game/project. Tutorial, wishlist-growth, Steam Next Fest signup, course, or generic developer-experience videos are research material, not CRM leads.
A valid first-pass lead does not require a Steam AppID. Bilibili videos, media articles, official sites, TapTap, indienova, or developer posts can be the first verification link.
Steam remains useful, but domestic developer Demo/test signals should outrank generic overseas upcoming lists.

Daily sourcing volume must not depend on Steam alone. When domestic media/Bilibili signals are healthy, the automation should produce a practical unprocessed review queue rather than one or two leads.
Expanded domestic media/Bilibili candidates may enter the unprocessed inbox when they clearly point to a game/product moment, even if the project name needs manual cleanup.
If Steam search or AppDetails is unavailable, the report must transparently fall back to domestic media/Bilibili review candidates rather than collapse to a token queue.
Bilibili expansion must filter stale videos, generic recommendation collections, mature blockbuster chatter, rant/review filler, and other non-actionable content.

Steam Trends must be a market board: category risers, Steam official/community windows, demo/Next Fest signals, publisher/developer slates, public data quality, and what those signals mean for Bilibili BD.
Industry radar should work as a China + overseas news board, not a short category filler list.

Industry radar should prioritize high-quality domestic and global sources when they reveal products, teams, publishing windows, legal/IP risk, creator momentum, market direction, platform policy, or Bilibili content angles.
Steam domestic keyword searches must use actual term filters and preserve the strongest domestic/Demo source for a repeated AppID.

Bilibili video leads must be enriched from video descriptions before CRM candidate creation, because descriptions often contain Steam store links, official sites, Discord, email, or other business-contact clues.

Bilibili recommendation videos are discovery signals only. Before creating a lead, search for and prefer official, developer, studio, or publisher Bilibili sources when they match the concrete project.
Steam, TapTap, official-site, and community links found in Bilibili descriptions, media bodies, gameplay text, or summaries must be extracted into structured links before validation and CRM sync.
Bilibili/media leads must be cross-checked against Steam when a Steam URL or AppID is present. Already released products must not enter push/watch review candidates.
Bilibili/media leads must dedupe against existing CRM projects, Steam AppIDs, source URLs, and normalized lead keys before creating a new candidate.
Bilibili video leads must be time-sensitive. Old videos should not create new review leads unless they contain a current playable/update/business window.

Media lead fields must stay decision-grade: priority_reason explains priority only, rule_fit explains why it fits or fails, gameplay is tag-like, progress is a short status, and next_action/notes are empty unless there is important extra evidence.

Low-volume backfill must never write automation bookkeeping, rule-version labels, or fallback diagnostics into user-facing lead fields such as notes, next_action, verdict, priority_reason, or rule_fit.
automation_guardrails: Fail fast when this rule file is missing or incompatible.
Log the active rule version at the start of each automation run.
Workflow path filters must include this file and SOURCING_RULES documents.
Rule iteration and online automation must be updated together.
Automatic daily reports must not pre-assign non-dropped leads to 观察池, 待评测, 跟进中, or 推进池; the human reviewer decides the bucket after reading.
The generator must not use already-launched Steam pools such as Popular New as CRM lead sources.
The generator must report both Steam candidate counts and media/Bilibili product-lead counts so low daily volume is diagnosable.
Low review volume must trigger fallback and diagnostics, not a full scheduled automation failure. Publish a low-volume but valid report when there are still effective candidates.
Domestic media/Bilibili under-conversion must be logged with source and filter diagnostics instead of silently collapsing to a Steam-only report.
The generator should dedupe against a meaningful recent report history window so stale items do not crowd out new discoveries.
The generator must inspect Bilibili video descriptions for Steam/contact links before deciding whether a Bilibili item is a new lead.
The generator must route Bilibili/media items with confirmed already-released Steam status to drop_pool or market background, not push/watch.
The generator log must include candidate total, duplicate filtered count, released filtered count, Bilibili official-source hits, and final non-dropped import candidates.
Only schema damage, file write failure, or CRM sync authentication/write failure should fail the scheduled automation.
GitHub Actions and Cloudflare sync paths must prefer CRM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN, with CRM_ACCESS_TOKEN only as a backwards-compatible fallback where explicitly supported.
Steam Trends must meet its item contract even when Steam sample quality is low by clearly marking domestic review-candidate fallback items.
Steam Trends market_insights must never use CRM Sourcing, rule documents, or internal automation notes as the source.
